summary:
Plot 0 follows the roof-height map: a 141-high pale limestone slab (with a penthouse to y 148) stepping down 132/105/59 toward Fifth Avenue, and a six-storey U podium plus Fifth Ave wings with roof gardens on setback decks at y 26. A stepped Deco portal frames the open forecourt where bronze ATLAS kneels under a 9-ring copper armillary sphere, between granite pylons. Atlas's real spot is in the notch at x 72..83, which is off the footprint, so the forecourt is pushed back to x 63..71 where the map shows a low 17-18 block. The British Empire Building and La Maison Française are identical six-storey twins with deeper setback storeys, gardened roofs and gilded relief panels over their Fifth Ave doors. Continuous piers, dark window strips, ~25% lit windows and floodlit setback decks make it read as Rockefeller Center from the air at dusk. Pale-buff limestone Art Deco ensemble in the architect's frames: stepped tower with floodlit penthouse, Fifth Ave wings with roof gardens, a portal framing the forecourt with bronze ATLAS under a copper armillary sphere, and the twin 6-storey Channel Gardens buildings.
Six parts: massing shell, portal and forecourt, Atlas, facades and lit fittings, roofs, gardens and lighting, final check. Dusk is carried by ~25% lit bays, lit shopfronts and lobby, and froglight-lit decks and crowns.

massing shell: parts/shell.mjs builds all masses for plots 0, 1 and 2 from a per-plot heightmap, and make.sh produces a whole build.nbt. `mcd check` reports 0 floating blocks. Nothing here was rendered or looked at, only checked.
Each mass is solid except a 3-deep air skin on every exposed face for the facade part. Edge parapets with slab coping sit at the deck. The 22/26 garden and ledge tops are left air for the roofs part. The portal, lobby and entrance recess cells are left empty.
polish: No render was made, so how the shell reads has not been seen. Only `mcd check` was run, and it reported 0 floating blocks with 4 orphans. `mcd fit` was not run.
I renamed roof.json to roof.json.unused. Its 'modern' preset made the roof tool clear 9038 shell cells, and build.mjs now skips the roof step. If a roof.json comes back, it must not strip the shell.
Facades must stop pier heads and glass at deck-2. The course at deck-1 is solid soffit, and the soffit also runs on into taller walls beside lower masses.

Deck tops at y22 and y26 are air except the edge parapet, so the roofs part must place the grass, gravel and deck_light at those levels. This covers GN, GS, the plot 1/2 U and GB gardens, SN/SS west of x58, and the ledges.
The P0 portal region x58..62 z20..35 and the lobby are empty. T1 at y19 and above over x58..61 hangs there until the portal part builds its piers and lintel.
The shell has no coat of cornice band at y22 on tall masses and no crown band at y139..142. Those belong to the facades part.
4 orphan blocks reported by `mcd check` were not examined.

waste.what: Working out the inset air skin, soffit course and parapet rules myself, in a heightmap script
waste.cost: about 4 retries, including floating cornice rings
waste.tool: A massing helper that takes a mass list and returns a solid core with a facade-ready skin of chosen depth, with parapets and an attached soffit

waste.what: Found that the architect's roof.json cleared the shell cells; I diagnosed it from the build log and moved the file aside
waste.cost: 1 rebuild
waste.tool: `mcd roof --dry-run` run when roof.json is written, to warn that it would clear the shell

companions.task: Quoins, a cornice band and pier heads at the soffit, and the moulded stepped edges of the setbacks
Check what the T1 y19-and-above hang over the empty portal and lobby box rests on, and check the soffit attachment of the cornice rings

summary:
portal and forecourt: Portal and forecourt built in parts/portal.mjs: E portal piers, lintel and coping at x 62, forecourt paving y 1 with smooth_stone joints, two granite pylons, Atlas plinth (y 2..5), and the lit lobby (froglight ceiling y 16, gold floor strip y 1).
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; the part places 872 blocks with 0 refused and 0 off-palette. Paving uplights were left to the Atlas part, as plan.md assigns them.
Ticked: plan.md Part 2 note, elements 4, 9, 11. Element 7 is only half done (plinth yes, figure no).
polish: ATLAS figure (elements 7, figure part) and the sphere are not built here: parts/atlas.mjs owns them, plus the paving uplights at (63,23), (63,32), (71,23), (71,32), (69,20), (69,35).

Shell orphans at 62,16,17 and 62,16,38 (smooth_sandstone sticking out at x 62 next to the portal, from the shell's C2/D2 wing abutments, not from this part). `$MCD check` reports them; the shell or finish part should fix them.
The lobby is lit and has a gold floor strip, but it is only visible through the portal glass once the facades part places glass at x 60, y 7..15, and the doors and gilded panels at x 61.
The lobby floor strip (gold_block at y 1, z 27..28, x 50..59) is an addition beyond elements.md; it is in plan.md's Notes so the facades or finish part can drop it if it reads wrong.
`$MCD walk` reports the build as not walkable end to end. That is outside this part, since the forecourt route is notional and the doors are not yet placed.

waste.what: Worked out the forecourt paving joints by hand: a double loop over x 63..71 and z 20..35 with g.set for each cell, computing joint positions from (x - x0) % 3 and (z - z0) % 3.
waste.cost: 144 cells set one by one in a loop, plus a check of the ground course at y 1 so the replacement lands on the ground layer rather than air.
waste.tool: A vocab `paving(g, box, { y, base, joint: 3, jointBlock })` helper that fills a box with a joint grid and reports which cells replaced ground, so this part does not hand-roll the loops.

waste.what: Found the reserved portal and lobby boxes and the ground-course writability rule by reading shell.mjs and the build library source, to confirm my helpers would write into air and not be refused.
waste.cost: Two source reads and a grep, about 3 tool calls, before the first build.
waste.tool: A `mcd reserved build.nbt --plot 0` or plan.md listing of each part's writable cells (air or ground course) so a worker can see the box it may write without reading the shell.

waste.what: Lobby ceiling and floor strip set cell by cell in double loops (120 froglight cells at y 16, 20 gold cells at y 1).
waste.cost: 140 g.set calls in code, no retries.
waste.tool: `fill` from the build library with a replace-only-ground option, or a `room_ceiling(g, box, y, block)` vocab helper.

waste.what: An uplight list I wrote and then removed: I first placed the six paving uplights before re-reading plan.md's ownership, which put them in the Atlas part, so a rebuild was needed.
waste.cost: One extra make.sh run and a code edit.
waste.tool: elements.md should name the owning part per uplight and per cell group (the table lists them only per element), so the workers don't overlap.

waste.what: Used sed -i with a script argument on macOS, which took the script as the backup suffix and failed.
waste.cost: One failed command and one retry.
waste.tool: Use the Edit tool for plan and elements ticks, not sed -i (macOS needs `sed -i ''`).

companions.task: Lay the E portal's piers, the chiseled lintel heads and the coping at x 62, and cut the granite plinth course and the Atlas plinth's stepped cap.
Set the forecourt paving at y 1 with its joint pattern and the granite pylon bases, and confirm the joint lines line up with the Atlas axis at z 27.5.
Place the paving uplights around the Atlas plinth and the pylon feet, so the figure is lit from below at dusk.
Glaze the portal windows at x 60 (y 7..15) and fit the bronze mullion frames so the lit lobby reads through them.

summary:
Atlas and armillary sphere: parts/atlas.mjs builds the plinth, two granite pylons, the kneeling atlas_figure, a four-ring armillary sphere centred (67,16,27.5) with axis and lightning-rod stubs, and six ochre uplights (679 blocks, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines).
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt at 03:31 with my part; `mcd check` reports no floating blocks from my part (4 orphans at x62 belong to the portal/shell).
The sphere reads only as a copper mass in the render, not as separate rings; the ecliptic is a local helper because vocab has no ring_tilted.
polish: Sphere legibility: at the Atlas close-up (render tiles-atlas/atlas.png) the four rings merge into one copper blob over the head; the spec's ~9-block hollow sphere is not clearly read. Needs a judgment call (ring thickness is fixed at 1 by the spec) or a review pass.
ring_tilted for the ecliptic is local to parts/atlas.mjs (function ringTilted); should move to vocab as a shared helper.

Uplights (63,1,23) (63,1,32) (71,1,23) (71,1,32) (69,1,20) (69,1,35) replace the paving/ground surface block; the portal part (0 placed in this run) must leave those cells as paving or air, or they stay plinth-coloured under the light.
atlas_figure gives only 3 waxed_weathered_cut_copper blocks (highlights are light against the ~20% upper bound); left as the vocab helper produced it.
elements.md has no status column, so items 7-10 are ticked only in plan.md's Part 3 line.

waste.what: Worked out the sphere's ring cells, ecliptic tilt vector and axis stub positions by hand, and wrote a local ringTilted sampler because vocab has no tilted-ring helper.
waste.cost: about 3 coordinate computations and one 900-step sampler; ~5 min of the 12-min budget
waste.tool: a vocab ring_tilted(g, centre, ex, u, a, b, mat) helper, plus an axis(g, p0, p1, mat, stubMat) helper with stubs beyond each end

waste.what: Judged whether the sphere reads by eye from several zoom and whole-site renders (east, north, atlas camera), since no tool reports whether a ring is visible at that scale.
waste.cost: 5 render calls, each a whole-site render of ~8 s; the result is still ambiguous
waste.tool: a mcd render option that reports a per-part silhouette or a ring-visibility count from a given camera, or a zoom with an elevation parameter

waste.what: Ticked plan.md and elements.md by appending a line to plan.md, because elements.md has no status column to tick.
waste.cost: one append; the item-by-item status had to be written as prose
waste.tool: a status column in elements.md (item | part | built yes/no), which the tick step could update with a single command

companions.task: Build the armature and proportions of the kneeling atlas_figure (arm reach to the sphere, bowed head, knee at x 69) before the blocks are placed, so the figure reads from the street at 12 blocks.
Lay out the four sphere rings and the ecliptic so they are separate hollow rings at a 9-block diameter, with clear gaps where the rings cross.
Cut and set the two pylons and the stepped plinth (polished deepslate base, andesite body, cap course) so the joints and the coping line up with the portal.
Place and check the six uplights so the figure and sphere are lit from below and no paving cell next to them is dark.

summary:
facades and fittings: parts/facades.mjs builds the piers and recessed glass strips on the exposed faces of all three plots, shopfronts with bronze fascias and lit back bays, the portal's three door pairs with tall glass and gilded panels, and the plot 1/2 Fifth Avenue ends with the relief panel and emblem.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt (facades: 18,902 placed, 2 refused writes into the shell, no off-palette blocks); check shows 0 floating and 0 unsupported blocks, and the street and forecourt render reads as stone piers and glass.
Not done: name boards, bronze door frames and lanterns, the setback and W/W2 facades, the plot 1/2 garden-door ramps, and the portal's own piers and lobby, which belong to the portal part.
polish: Shop name boards not placed: plaque() was not called, so no fascia reads a name (element 13). Needs a 2-row band or a banner board on the fascia.
bronze_door frames and the lanterns beside each door are not built: the helper writes lanterns one cell outside the plot on north/south faces, so doors are plain dark_oak pairs (element 6 partly).
Plot 1/2 garden shop doors at x 26..27 sit on ground 1 and need a 2-cell slab ramp to reach floor 2; not placed (doors are at y 3..4 with no step).
Setback storeys (SN/SS, IN/IS), plot 1/2 setback U and the W/W2 west towers have no facade pieces yet; only the long faces, the east ends and the Fifth Avenue wings are faced.
2 writes refused into the shell at (31,5,1) and (32,5,1): the shell holds smooth_sandstone where the C1 shopfront glass should be.
Portal glass and gilded panels sit against piers the portal part has not built yet; check orphans at (61,19,23..32) and (62,16..18) after the merge.
elements.md has no tick boxes, so the ticks are recorded as notes in plan.md's Part 4 line.

waste.what: Shopfront and portal door placement, done one door cell at a time with g.set (two leaves and two halves per door, about 12 calls across the faces).
waste.cost: about 30 door cells hand-set with the same lower/upper/hinge pattern
waste.tool: A vocab door-pair helper that sets both leaves and halves on a face, with the lanterns left out where they would fall outside the plot. I wrote doorPair() locally.

waste.what: Finding the pier residue for each plot by hand: plot origin plus local pier column, mod 3, plus the sign for each face's outward direction.
waste.cost: three arithmetic retries (the first pierMod was in local x, not kit x)
waste.tool: pier_strip_face could take the plot-local frame (origin and local pier residue) so the caller never converts kit and local coordinates.

waste.what: Checking whether each shop bay's display candle had a floor under it, by scanning the grid after building.
waste.cost: one check run, then a post-pass to add a floor block under each candle over air
waste.tool: shop_bay could place its own floor course at y1 under the display row, so it is supported as it is written.

waste.what: Reading the render to see whether the facade reads: looked at the street view and the front-right view by eye only.
waste.cost: 2 renders
waste.tool: mcd card --layout eye on the facade alone would give one image instead of several separate tiles.

companions.task: Letter the shop name boards on each fascia (a 2-row banner band or a block-letter plaque on the bronze), and the Fifth Avenue entrance signage, so no fascia is left blank.
Check the 2-cell slab ramp at the plot 1/2 garden doors and the portal's coping and reveals, so the limestone joins are right at the door heads.
Set the shopfront and portal glass connection states and the bronze mullion frames at x 60/61, and check the lit glass rows.

summary:
roofs, gardens and lighting: Part 5 (parts/roofs.mjs) is built: every open garden and ledge top is planted, roof gardens GN, GS and both GB gardens are laid, and every smooth_stone deck is lit. make.sh runs clean (0 refused, 0 off-palette), and `mcd check` shows no floating blocks.
Deck lights are lanterns standing on the deck, not flush froglights, because runParts locks the shell's deck cells and refused all 192 flush lights. Measured block light on the roof rooms is min 4 (no dark deck cell).
Two gaps remain: the E portal roof's froglights are not placed (the portal part owns that cell), and the plot 0 x58..61 z12..17 corner has no support under it, so it is left as air.
polish: Deck lights are standing lanterns (hanging false) on each deck cell, not the flush ochre_froglight the ROOFS table asks for: runParts refuses any write into the shell's deck cells, so every flush light was refused. Flush lights need runParts to allow replacing a flush surface block, or the shell to leave the lattice cells as air.
The E portal roof (deck 17, portal part's cells) gets no froglights from this part: the 2 lights lighting T1's face are not placed. The portal part must add them.
Plot 0 x58..61 z12..17 has no mass under it (no garden there; the GN garden is x62..81 only), so it is left air. A supported deck is needed there if the plan's GN box is meant to cover it.

The plot 1/2 ledges are one cell wide (the shell puts the parapet and coping on the outer cell), so ledge_planter's two-row hedge does not fit; I used the generic grass, hedge and lamp-post pass instead. The 2-wide planted ledges in the plan are not built as drawn.
The ROOFS table's PH corner floodlights are not placed as corner blocks; they are lattice lanterns on the PH deck.
The vents are slab pairs with iron-bar grilles (plan says stone_stairs, not in the palette): (10,7,2) and (16,7,5) on the A roof.

mcd check reports 4 orphan blocks at (62,16,17), (62,18,20), (62,18,35) and (62,16,38): these are the portal and shell edge at x62, not this part's cells, and need the portal or facade part to resolve.
elements.md has no checkbox column, so I did not tick its rows; the Part 5 tick and the deviations are recorded in plan.md's checklist and Notes instead.
Visual check was a whole-site sheet only (roof-sheet.png, front-left iso): the gardens and ledges read as planted and the decks show, but I did not zoom in on the lanterns or the vents.

waste.what: Hand-worked which open roof cells were gardens, gravel, grass or ledge: I reasoned from the shell's top heights, edges and supporting masses cell by cell instead of asking a tool for the open deck cells.
waste.cost: about 15 minutes of reasoning and 3 failed garden boxes (roof_garden spilled over the box, the 4-wide GN/GS strips were too small)
waste.tool: A build-library helper `openDeck(g, y, {region})` that returns cells with air at the top course and solid below, grouped into rectangles with their edge flags, would have replaced the hand scan.

waste.what: Deck lighting: the flush ochre_froglight deck_light helper writes into shell-owned smooth_stone, which runParts' lock refuses, so I had to switch to standing lanterns after one full build.
waste.cost: one failed make.sh run and one rebuild (192 refused writes)
waste.tool: runParts should let a part replace a flush surface block (the helper's own FLUSH_OK contract), or deck_light should take the shell's deck as an allowed surface; a `deckLights(g, box, y, spacing)` helper would also cover the lattice plus gap fill I wrote by hand.

waste.what: Light checking needed a hand-written rooms file for each roof level, because `mcd light --y` printed no summary without rooms.
waste.cost: one rooms file of 10 boxes, plus two wrong box orders fixed by hand
waste.tool: `mcd light --y <y> --box x0,z0,x1,z1` summarising min/mean/dark per box without a rooms file.

waste.what: The vent helper uses stone_stairs, which is not in the palette, so I wrote a local slab-pair vent instead.
waste.cost: one local helper of 5 lines
waste.tool: Add stone_stairs (or a smooth_stone slab variant) to palette.json, or let the vent helper take its block as an option.

companions.task: Plant the roof gardens and ledges: the hedge line along the coping, the gravel path rings and cross paths, the flower beds, and the lamp-post spacing, so I would not have to lay out the beds by hand.
Set the lantern lattice on every deck and check the dark cells with a light map per roof, choosing the spacing that keeps every deck cell at 8 or more.
Own the deck and coping courses of the setbacks, the vent placement on the A roof, and the lead-free flashing where the roofs meet by abutment.

summary:
final check: parts/finish.mjs written: runs last and reports height, plot-bounds and pane-connection problems (locked cells, so reported not fixed), then lights every sky-open walkable cell with no lamp within 7 Manhattan blocks using standing lanterns on air cells only.
Ran ./make.sh: build.nbt saved (267,567 blocks, 253 lanterns from this pass on the shell-only build), with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines; mcd check shows 0 floating, 4 orphans at x62 from the shell's portal face, and mcd fit OK.
Light coverage is true by construction for the sky-open cells at the time of the pass; I did not measure it with mcd light, which needs rooms. The pass must rerun after the other parts merge (make.sh does this).
polish: Only the massing shell existed in this copy, so the lamp pass lit shell-level surfaces only; the final lamp count and placement must be re-checked after the roof, facade and portal parts merge (make.sh reruns it).
Shell orphans at x=62 (z 16..17, 20, 35, 38; y 16..18) stick out from the portal face: the portal part (x 58..62) must fill or close them.
Pane connection states were checked but no panes exist yet, so the pane check is unexercised; a future facade pass must set them.

Lanterns are standing on any sky-open walkable air cell, including street-level cells in front of shopfronts; the facade and portal parts should be inspected for lamps that land in shop-window or door lanes.
The light check is by construction, not measured: mcd light needs rooms.json rooms, so no walkable-surface light map was produced.

waste.what: Checking light coverage across the whole build had no tool: I wrote a greedy sky-open-surface sweep in finish.mjs by hand, computing Manhattan distances against every lamp.
waste.cost: about 4 minutes of writing and rerunning make.sh; the sweep is O(surfaces x lamps) with a plain array scan
waste.tool: an `mcd light --walkable` mode that maps every sky-open walkable cell of the build, not only rooms.json rooms, would replace the hand sweep and measure what it claims

waste.what: Working out which sky-open cells are walkable and which lie inside the lot by hand, using plotOf and onLot offsets.
waste.cost: a few retries on the local-coordinate offsets
waste.tool: a vocab helper plotOf(x,z) returning {plot, lx, lz} from PLOT_ORIGIN/PLOT_SIZE would remove the per-part offset arithmetic

waste.what: Checking pane connection states by hand: a neighbour-by-neighbour comparison in the sweep, with no way to correct locked panes.
waste.cost: one function of about 15 lines; no panes present to test it against
waste.tool: `mcd check --panes` that reports pane states that disagree with their neighbours, plus a deterministic pane-state setter that a facade part can call

companions.task: Plant beds and hedges first, so the lamp sweep puts lanterns in the gravel paths and clear deck cells, not in flower beds or under the tree crowns.
Set pane connections on the facade glass and the portal windows, so the pane check in finish.mjs passes without manual state fixes.
Close the shell's portal-face orphans at x=62 with the right limestone course or slab, so the structure check is clean before the lamp pass.

summary: inspection: Fixed the seven FIT 'bottom slab' issues: A-roof vent bases (4 iron bars) are now full smooth_stone blocks, and the GS coping under the tree crown at x 71..73, z 38 is a full limestone course (3 leaves). make.sh builds build.nbt; walk ok (1877 cells reached, no unreachable rooms); fit OK.

waste.what: Traced the oak_leaves source by hand: the FIT line gives cells but not the placing module, so I grepped for the block name, found only the iron_bars in roofs.mjs, then read the roof_garden tree geometry in vocab/h2.mjs to work out that the crown row at z 38 comes from the tree centred at z 40 and that the coping slab is shell.mjs's edge course at y 27.
waste.cost: about 6 tool calls and two file reads to locate 7 cells
waste.tool: FIT lines should name the placing module and helper (e.g. 'placed by parts/shell.mjs coping edge, or vocab roof_garden tree crown'); 'fit --json' could report the writer of each cell

waste.what: Worked out the crown extent (which dy and dv rows of the tree reach z 38 at x 71..73) by reading the tree loop instead of reading the cells' own writers.
waste.cost: one read plus mental geometry
waste.tool: a per-cell writer log from runParts (part name and helper) would show this directly
